teach_overlay.label: Yogurt bacteria snip viruses
teach_overlay.timeline_step: 3/4 · 23 Mar 2007 (Rodolphe Barrangou & Philippe Horvath prove yogurt bacteria use CRISPR-Cas9 as an adaptive immune system)

plates.side_label: 23 MAR 2007 BARRANGOU & HORVATH: +1 VIRAL SPACER = 10^5× RESISTANCE, +2–4 SPACERS = >10^7× RESISTANCE (CAS9 REQUIRED)
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Streptococcus thermophilus phage-resistance & spacer-acquisition chart from Barrangou, Fremaux, Deveau, Richards, Boyaval, Moineau, Romero & Horvath (23 March 2007, Science 315: 1709–1712) shows phage sensitivity dropping 10^5-fold with 1 acquired 30-bp viral spacer and >10^7-fold with 2–4 spacers while cas9 (cas5) inactivation abolishes immunity.

teach_overlay.label: 23 MAR 2007 YOGURT CRISPR PROOF: +1 SPACER CUTS PHAGE INFECTION 100,000× (10^5); +2–4 SPACERS CUT >10,000,000× (10^7)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Streptococcus thermophilus phage-resistance & spacer-acquisition chart on period paper from Barrangou, Fremaux, Deveau, Richards, Boyaval, Moineau, Romero & Horvath (23 March 2007, Science 315: 1709–1712) showing phage sensitivity dropping 10^5-fold with 1 acquired 30-bp viral spacer and >10^7-fold with 2–4 spacers while cas9 (cas5) inactivation abolishes immunity
teach_overlay.scale: adding just one thirty-letter viral mugshot to a yogurt bacterium's CRISPR archive cuts virus infection a hundred thousand times — and every daughter cell inherits that shield the moment it divides
